Method of Attack: Adware behavior hidden until verification by checking if device IP belongs to Google, remaining silent if true
24-minute delay before showing first ad to evade typical app testing
Showing shortcut icon to mislead users uninstalling app (only deletes shortcut, app runs in background)
Mimicking legitimate apps from Facebook or Google to conceal origin of ads
Displaying Facebook or Google icon in Recent Apps list to hide real app name
Discoverer: Lukas Stefanko, mobile malware researcher at ESET
Attack Vector: Malicious apps distributed via Google Play Store
Indicators of Compromise: Domain minigameshouse.us used for adware command and control communication
Domain minigameshouse.net linked to Facebook page Minigameshouse
Registration details including phone number matching Facebook profile and domain registration
42 malicious apps discovered in Google Play Store
One app with over five million installations and about 87,000 reviews averaging 4.2 rating
Date of Discovery: Reported in blog post today (relative to source content)
